courses.title: Basic Electronics
topics: Semiconductor physics: energy bands, carriers, n and p material
Diodes: bias, V-I curve, Zener, rectifiers, filters, regulated supplies, clippers, clampers, multipliers, datasheets
BJT: operation, CE/CB/CC, load line, biasing, thermal stability, switching

courses.description: From the physics of silicon to working amplifier and logic circuits, with every circuit built, measured and simulated rather than only drawn. Taught to the depth of a first-year engineering circuits course, with every circuit simulated and measured.
modelledOn: Sedra and Smith, Microelectronic Circuits
Agarwal and Lang, Foundations of Analog and Digital Electronic Circuits
Boylestad and Nashelsky, Electronic Devices and Circuit Theory
outcomes: Analyse DC and AC circuits with Kirchhoff's laws, node and mesh analysis, Thevenin and Norton equivalents.
Explain how carriers move in doped silicon and derive the diode and transistor V-I behaviour from it.
Design rectifiers, regulators, clippers and clampers and predict their waveforms.
Bias a BJT amplifier for stable operation and compute its gain, input and output resistance.
Analyse RLC circuits in the time and frequency domains and read resonance and bandwidth from a plot.
Classify signals and relate the continuous and discrete views of them to later signal processing courses.

syllabus.title: Circuit fundamentals and lab practice

Resistors, Ohm's law, series and parallel combinations, voltage and current dividers
Kirchhoff's current and voltage laws; node-voltage and mesh-current analysis
Superposition, Thevenin and Norton equivalents, maximum power transfer
Using a breadboard, multimeter, oscilloscope and bench supply; reading a datasheet
Dependent sources and the ideal operational amplifier as a circuit element

syllabus.title: Semiconductor physics

Clippers, clampers and voltage multipliers; LED and photodiode circuits

syllabus.title: Bipolar junction transistors

Common-emitter, common-base and common-collector configurations and their characteristics
DC load line and Q-point; fixed, emitter and voltage-divider biasing; bias stability and thermal runaway
Small-signal model (hybrid-pi) and the gain, input and output resistance of a CE amplifier
The transistor as a switch: driving an LED, a relay and a small DC motor
Introduction to MOSFETs: enhancement-mode NMOS and PMOS, threshold voltage, regions of operation

syllabus.title: Operational amplifiers

Comparators, Schmitt triggers and simple oscillators

CMOS inverter, NAND and NOR; static and dynamic power

courses.description: The mathematics that computer science is written in: logic, proof, sets, relations, counting, number theory and graphs, taught by proving and computing rather than memorising. Taught to the depth of the standard mathematics-for-computer-science course, with every proof technique practised on real problems.
modelledOn: Rosen, Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
Lehman, Leighton and Meyer, Mathematics for Computer Science
Epp, Discrete Mathematics with Applications
outcomes: Translate English statements into propositional and predicate logic and check validity with truth tables and inference rules.
Write correct proofs by direct argument, contrapositive, contradiction, cases and induction, including strong and structural induction.
Work fluently with sets, functions and relations, and prove properties such as injectivity, equivalence and partial order.
Count arrangements with permutations, combinations, the pigeonhole principle and inclusion-exclusion, and solve recurrences.
Apply modular arithmetic, GCD and the Chinese remainder theorem, including to RSA.
Model problems as graphs and reason about paths, trees, colourings and planarity.

Predicates and quantifiers; nested quantifiers; negating quantified statements
Normal forms (CNF, DNF) and satisfiability; logic puzzles

Proof that the square root of 2 is irrational; infinitude of primes

Recursive algorithms and proving them correct; towers of Hanoi, merge sort recurrence

courses.description: A whole-degree tour of what a computer is, how information is represented and moved, and what computing does to society, so that every later course has a map to hang on. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory computer science survey, with hands-on exercises for every idea.
modelledOn: Brookshear and Brylow, Computer Science: An Overview
Schneider and Gersting, Invitation to Computer Science
Petzold, Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software

Represent text, numbers, images and sound in binary and estimate storage and bandwidth needs.
Explain what algorithms, programs, operating systems and compilers are and how they fit together.
Organise information in files, spreadsheets and relational databases and query it.
Explain how the Internet and the Web work end to end, from a URL to a rendered page.
Reason about safety, privacy, ethics and the social impact of computing with Ghanaian and global examples.

courses.description: First contact with programming: thinking in algorithms, writing them as pseudocode and flowcharts, then as real code with variables, control flow, functions and a first look at objects. Taught to the depth of a leading first programming course, with a working program every week.

Guttag, Introduction to Computation and Programming
Roberts, The Art and Science of Java

topics: Matrix operations, solving systems, determinants, inverses and eigen-decomposition in both tools
Plotting functions, curves, vectors and transformations
Fitting a line to data by least squares as a matrix problem
A capstone: image transformation or a simple recommendation using vector similarity

courses.title: Probability and Statistics
topics: Probability theory
Random variables
Special distributions
Moments and moment generating functions
Special probability theorems
Joint probability distributions
Computer simulation in R
courses.description: Probability theory and statistics built for computer scientists, with every distribution simulated in R before and after it is derived. Taught to the depth of a full probability course for computer scientists.
modelledOn: Ross, A First Course in Probability
Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis, Introduction to Probability
Walpole, Myers, Myers and Ye, Probability and Statistics for Engineers and Scientists
outcomes: Compute probabilities of events with counting, conditional probability, independence and Bayes' theorem.
Work with discrete and continuous random variables, their PMFs, PDFs, CDFs, expectations and variances.
Recognise and apply the standard distributions, including Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, Poisson, uniform, exponential and normal.
Use moments and moment generating functions to derive properties and sums of random variables.
Apply the law of large numbers and central limit theorem and construct confidence intervals and hypothesis tests.
Simulate random processes in R and use the results to check analytic answers and estimate hard quantities.

syllabus.title: Probability theory
topics: Sample spaces, events, set operations; axioms of probability
Counting: permutations, combinations, multinomials; birthday problem and hash collisions
Conditional probability, multiplication rule, law of total probability
Bayes' theorem: medical tests, spam filters, malaria rapid tests with false positives
Independence and conditional independence; reliability of series and parallel systems

syllabus.title: Random variables
topics: Discrete random variables, probability mass functions, cumulative distribution functions
Continuous random variables, probability density functions; the CDF as the bridge
Expectation, variance, standard deviation; linearity of expectation
Functions of random variables; expectation of a function
Indicator variables and counting with expectation (expected number of collisions, fixed points)

syllabus.title: Special distributions
topics: Bernoulli, binomial, geometric, negative binomial, hypergeometric
Poisson distribution and the Poisson process: arrivals at a bank, packets at a router
Uniform, exponential (memorylessness) and gamma distributions
Normal distribution: standardisation, tables, the 68-95-99.7 rule; normal approximation to binomial
Choosing a distribution for a real situation; fitting and checking in R

syllabus.title: Moments and moment generating functions
topics: Moments about the origin and about the mean; skewness and kurtosis
Moment generating functions: definition, computing moments, uniqueness
MGFs of the standard distributions; sums of independent random variables
Characteristic functions and probability generating functions in brief

syllabus.title: Joint probability distributions
topics: Joint, marginal and conditional distributions for discrete and continuous pairs
Independence of random variables; covariance and correlation
Conditional expectation and the law of iterated expectation
Sums of random variables, convolution; distribution of the maximum and minimum
Bivariate normal distribution; transformations of two variables

syllabus.title: Special probability theorems
topics: Markov and Chebyshev inequalities; Chernoff bounds for randomised algorithms
Weak and strong laws of large numbers
Central limit theorem: statement, intuition and simulation
Applications: Monte Carlo estimation, error in polling, load on a server

syllabus.title: Statistics: estimation and testing
topics: Descriptive statistics, histograms, boxplots, sample mean and variance
Point estimation: method of moments, maximum likelihood; bias and consistency
Confidence intervals for means and proportions; t-distribution
Hypothesis testing: null and alternative, p-values, type I and II errors, z and t tests, chi-square tests
Simple linear regression and correlation; A/B testing a web page

syllabus.title: Computer simulation in R
topics: Pseudo-random numbers; sample, runif, rnorm, rbinom and friends; setting seeds
Simulating games, queues and random walks; estimating probabilities and expectations
Inverse transform and rejection sampling to generate any distribution
Bootstrap confidence intervals; visualising sampling distributions
Project: simulate a mobile-money transaction system or a classroom's exam scores and compare with theory

courses.title: Programming with C
topics: C syntax, types and operators
Control flow and functions
Arrays and strings
Pointers and memory
Structures and unions
File handling
The preprocessor and compilation
courses.description: C as the language of the machine: types, pointers, memory, structures, files and the toolchain, taught by writing and debugging real systems-style programs. Taught to the depth of a leading systems programming course.
modelledOn: Kernighan and Ritchie, The C Programming Language
Bryant and O'Hallaron, Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (C and memory chapters)
King, C Programming: A Modern Approach
outcomes: Write well-structured C programs using the full type system, operators, control flow and functions.
Use arrays, strings and pointers correctly and explain their representation in memory.
Allocate and free dynamic memory and build linked structures without leaks or dangling pointers.
Model data with structures, unions and enumerations and persist it with text and binary files.
Drive the preprocessor, compiler, linker and debugger, and split a program across multiple files.
Find memory errors with tools such as a debugger and a sanitizer and reason about undefined behaviour.

syllabus.title: C syntax, types and operators
topics: A first program; compiling with gcc or clang; the structure of a C program
Integer, character and floating types; sizes, ranges, signedness, overflow, limits.h
Constants, variables, declarations, initialisation; const and typedef
Arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise and assignment operators; precedence; implicit conversions
printf and scanf formatting; getchar and putchar

syllabus.title: Control flow and functions
topics: if, switch, while, do-while, for; break, continue, goto
Function definition and declaration, prototypes, header files
Call by value; scope, storage classes (auto, static, extern, register)
Recursion and the call stack; stack frames
Modular design: splitting a program into functions and files

syllabus.title: Arrays and strings
topics: One- and multi-dimensional arrays; initialisation; array bounds and the danger of overrun
Strings as null-terminated char arrays; string.h functions and writing your own strlen, strcpy, strcmp
Passing arrays to functions; sizeof pitfalls
Sorting and searching arrays; a word-count and a Caesar cipher program

syllabus.title: Pointers and memory
topics: Addresses, the & and * operators, pointer types, NULL
Pointer arithmetic and the equivalence of arrays and pointers; pointers to pointers
Call by reference with pointers; returning multiple values; swap
The memory map of a process: text, data, BSS, heap, stack
Dynamic memory: malloc, calloc, realloc, free; leaks, double free, use after free
Linked lists, stacks and a binary tree with dynamic nodes
Function pointers and callbacks; qsort

syllabus.title: Structures, unions and enumerations
topics: Defining and using struct; nested structures; arrays of structures; the arrow operator
Memory layout, padding and alignment
Unions and tagged unions; bit fields; enum
Structures as records: a student register and an inventory program

syllabus.title: File handling
topics: Streams: stdin, stdout, stderr; fopen, fclose and modes
Text I/O: fgets, fputs, fprintf, fscanf; line-by-line processing
Binary I/O: fread, fwrite, fseek, ftell; writing and reading records
Error handling with errno and perror; checking return values
Command-line arguments and processing a CSV file of sales data

syllabus.title: The preprocessor and compilation
topics: #include, #define, macros with arguments and their pitfalls, conditional compilation, include guards
The pipeline: preprocessing, compilation, assembly, linking; object files and libraries
Makefiles and building multi-file projects; static and shared libraries
Compiler flags, warnings as errors and optimisation levels

syllabus.title: Debugging, safety and undefined behaviour
topics: gdb: breakpoints, stepping, inspecting memory and the stack
AddressSanitizer and Valgrind for leaks and invalid accesses
Undefined behaviour: uninitialised variables, signed overflow, buffer overflow and why it matters for security
Defensive coding, assertions and unit tests in C
Project: a small system utility or data manager combining files, structs and pointers

courses.title: Calculus
topics: Differential calculus
Integral calculus
Approximate integration
Partial differentiation
Multiple integrals and volumes
First-order differential equations and applications
Applications in R and/or MATLAB
courses.description: Single-variable and introductory multivariable calculus with differential equations, taught with R and MATLAB alongside the pen so that every technique is also computed and plotted. Taught to the depth of a full first-year calculus sequence.
modelledOn: Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals
Strang, Calculus
Thomas, Calculus
outcomes: Compute limits and derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions and apply them to rates, optimisation and curve sketching.
Evaluate definite and indefinite integrals by substitution, parts, partial fractions and trigonometric methods, and apply them to area, volume and average value.
Approximate integrals numerically with the trapezoidal and Simpson rules and bound the error.
Differentiate functions of several variables, find gradients, and locate and classify extrema.
Set up and evaluate double and triple integrals for areas, volumes and masses.
Solve first-order differential equations analytically and numerically and model growth, decay and cooling.

syllabus.title: Functions, limits and continuity
topics: Review of functions, graphs, polynomials, rational, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Limits: intuition, one-sided limits, limit laws, squeeze theorem; limits at infinity
Continuity, types of discontinuity, intermediate value theorem
Plotting functions and estimating limits in R and MATLAB

syllabus.title: Differential calculus
topics: Derivative as a limit, as slope and as rate of change; differentiability
Rules: power, product, quotient, chain; implicit and logarithmic differentiation
Derivatives of trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Applications: related rates, linear approximation, l'Hopital's rule
Mean value theorem; increasing and decreasing functions; concavity and curve sketching
Optimisation: maximising profit for a market stall, minimising material for a tank
Newton's method and symbolic differentiation in software

syllabus.title: Integral calculus
topics: Antiderivatives and the indefinite integral; Riemann sums and the definite integral
Fundamental theorem of calculus
Substitution, integration by parts, trigonometric integrals and substitutions
Partial fractions and integration of rational functions
Improper integrals
Applications: area between curves, volumes of revolution, arc length, average value, work

syllabus.title: Approximate integration
topics: Midpoint, trapezoidal and Simpson's rules
Error bounds and choosing the number of subintervals
Implementing the rules in R and MATLAB and comparing with built-in integrators
Taylor and Maclaurin series; using series to approximate integrals

syllabus.title: Partial differentiation
topics: Functions of two and three variables; level curves and surfaces
Partial derivatives, higher-order partials, Clairaut's theorem
Tangent planes, differentials and the chain rule for several variables
Gradient and directional derivatives
Local extrema, second-derivative test, Lagrange multipliers

syllabus.title: Multiple integrals and volumes
topics: Double integrals over rectangles and general regions; changing the order of integration
Double integrals in polar coordinates
Triple integrals; cylindrical and spherical coordinates
Applications: volume, mass, centre of mass, surface area

syllabus.title: First-order differential equations
topics: Modelling with differential equations; direction fields
Separable and linear first-order equations; integrating factors; exact equations
Applications: population growth and logistic models, radioactive decay, Newton's law of cooling, mixing problems, RC circuits
Euler's method and Runge-Kutta in R and MATLAB; comparing numeric and exact solutions
A glimpse of second-order equations and oscillation

courses.title: Computer Networking I
topics: Introduction to networking
OSI and TCP/IP models, protocols
IPv4 addressing and subnetting
Components and devices
Installation and configuration
Cabling and wiring, wireless
Network management
Network security
Error detection and correction
courses.description: How networks are built and why they work: the layered models, IPv4 addressing and subnetting, the devices and cabling of a LAN, and the first steps in managing and securing one. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory networking course and the first half of the industry routing-and-switching certification.
modelledOn: Kurose and Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
Cisco CCNA 200-301 network fundamentals and access objectives
Tanenbaum and Wetherall, Computer Networks
outcomes: Explain the OSI and TCP/IP models and place every common protocol and device at its layer.
Design IPv4 addressing plans with classless subnetting and VLSM and verify them by hand and with tools.
Build, cable and configure a small wired and wireless LAN with switches, a router and DHCP.
Explain how Ethernet, ARP, IP, TCP, UDP, DNS and HTTP cooperate to deliver a web page.
Detect and correct transmission errors with parity, CRC and checksums.
Monitor a network with ping, traceroute, Wireshark and SNMP and apply basic security controls.

syllabus.title: Introduction to networking
topics: What a network is; hosts, links, switches, routers; LAN, MAN, WAN, PAN; topologies
Circuit switching versus packet switching; delay, loss, throughput, bandwidth-delay product
The Internet as a network of networks: ISPs, IXPs (including GIX in Accra), submarine cables
Network performance measurement with ping and iperf

syllabus.title: OSI and TCP/IP models and protocols
topics: The seven OSI layers and the four TCP/IP layers; encapsulation and headers
Protocols, services and interfaces; the end-to-end principle
Application layer: HTTP, DNS, SMTP, FTP, SSH; sockets
Transport layer: TCP connection setup, reliability, flow and congestion control; UDP
Network layer: IP forwarding, routers and routing tables; ICMP
Following one HTTP request through every layer in Wireshark

syllabus.title: IPv4 addressing and subnetting
topics: Binary and dotted decimal; classful history; private and public addresses; special addresses
Subnet masks, CIDR notation, network and broadcast addresses, usable hosts
Fixed-length and variable-length subnetting (VLSM); designing a plan for a campus
Supernetting and route summarisation
IPv6: address format, types, SLAAC, dual stack
ARP, DHCP and how a host gets on the network

syllabus.title: Data link layer and Ethernet
topics: Framing, MAC addresses, Ethernet frame format
Shared media and CSMA/CD; full duplex; hubs versus switches
Switch learning, forwarding and flooding; the MAC table; spanning tree in brief
Link-layer tools: ipconfig, arp, switch show commands

syllabus.title: Error detection and correction
topics: Bit errors and burst errors; Hamming distance
Parity, two-dimensional parity, Internet checksum
Cyclic redundancy check: polynomial division and hardware implementation
Forward error correction with Hamming codes; ARQ: stop-and-wait, go-back-N, selective repeat

syllabus.title: Components and devices
topics: NICs, repeaters, hubs, bridges, switches (managed and unmanaged), routers, access points, firewalls
Layer-3 switches, modems, ONTs and the devices in a Ghanaian home or office connection
Reading device specifications: ports, speeds, PoE, throughput
Network diagrams and documentation

syllabus.title: Cabling, wiring and wireless
topics: Twisted pair categories (Cat5e, Cat6, Cat6a), T568A/B, straight-through and crossover; crimping and testing
Fibre optics: single-mode and multi-mode, connectors, attenuation; coaxial
Structured cabling: patch panels, racks, labelling, cable management
Wi-Fi standards (802.11 a/b/g/n/ac/ax), channels, interference, site survey, mesh
Wireless security: WPA2, WPA3, enterprise authentication

syllabus.title: Installation and configuration
topics: Configuring a switch and a router from the CLI: hostnames, interfaces, IP addresses, default gateway
Setting up DHCP and DNS forwarding on a small router; static addressing for servers and printers
Configuring a wireless access point; guest networks
Connectivity testing: ping, traceroute, nslookup, netstat; a fault-finding procedure

syllabus.title: Network management
topics: Monitoring: SNMP, syslog, NetFlow; interface counters and utilisation graphs
Packet capture and analysis with Wireshark
Change management, backups of configurations, documentation, IP address management
Troubleshooting methodology layer by layer

syllabus.title: Network security
topics: Threats: sniffing, spoofing, man-in-the-middle, denial of service, rogue DHCP
Access control: passwords, SSH instead of Telnet, port security, MAC filtering
Firewalls, NAT as a side effect, basic packet filtering
Security policies for a school or small business network

courses.title: Data Communications
topics: Signals, bandwidth and noise
Analog and digital transmission
Line coding and modulation
Multiplexing
Error detection and correction
Flow control and switching
Transmission media
courses.description: The physical and link layers in depth: how bits become signals, survive noise and bandwidth limits, share a medium, and arrive without error. Taught to the depth of a leading digital communication systems course.
modelledOn: Forouzan, Data Communications and Networking
Stallings, Data and Computer Communications
Proakis and Salehi, Fundamentals of Communication Systems
outcomes: Describe signals in time and frequency, compute bandwidth, and apply the Nyquist and Shannon limits to a channel.
Explain and simulate line codes and analog and digital modulation schemes and their trade-offs.
Design multiplexing schemes (FDM, TDM, WDM, CDM) for a given set of channels.
Compute and implement error detection and correction codes and evaluate their power.
Analyse flow-control protocols and compare circuit, packet and message switching.
Choose a transmission medium for a link given distance, bandwidth, cost and environment.

syllabus.title: Data communication fundamentals
topics: Components of a communication system: source, transmitter, channel, receiver, destination
Simplex, half-duplex, full-duplex; serial and parallel; synchronous and asynchronous
Protocols and standards bodies: ITU-T, IEEE, IETF, ISO
Where this course sits: physical and data-link layers of the OSI model

syllabus.title: Signals, bandwidth and noise
topics: Analog and digital signals; periodic signals; amplitude, frequency, phase, wavelength
Time and frequency domains; Fourier series and the spectrum of a square wave; composite signals
Bandwidth of a signal and of a channel; baseband and passband
Transmission impairments: attenuation, distortion, noise (thermal, crosstalk, impulse); decibels and SNR
Nyquist bit rate and Shannon capacity; computing the capacity of a telephone line and a Wi-Fi channel
Throughput, latency, jitter and bandwidth-delay product

syllabus.title: Analog and digital transmission
topics: Digital-to-digital, analog-to-digital, digital-to-analog and analog-to-analog conversion as a map
Sampling theorem, quantisation, PCM and delta modulation; voice at 64 kbit/s
Transmission modes: parallel, serial asynchronous, serial synchronous, isochronous
Baud rate versus bit rate; signal element versus data element

syllabus.title: Line coding and modulation
topics: Line coding requirements: DC balance, clock recovery, bandwidth; NRZ, NRZ-I, Manchester, differential Manchester, AMI, 4B/5B, 8B/10B
Block coding and scrambling
Digital-to-analog modulation: ASK, FSK, PSK, QPSK, QAM; constellation diagrams; bits per symbol
Analog modulation: AM, FM, PM and radio broadcasting
Simulating modulation and demodulation in software and observing the effect of noise

syllabus.title: Multiplexing and spreading
topics: Frequency-division multiplexing; guard bands; radio and cable TV
Wavelength-division multiplexing in fibre
Time-division multiplexing: synchronous and statistical; T1/E1 framing
Code-division multiplexing and orthogonal codes
Spread spectrum: frequency hopping and direct sequence

syllabus.title: Transmission media
topics: Guided media: twisted pair, coaxial, optical fibre; construction, bandwidth, attenuation, cost
Unguided media: radio, microwave, satellite, infrared; propagation modes and antennas
Comparing media for a rural school link: fibre, point-to-point wireless, satellite, 4G
Connectors and interfaces: RS-232, USB, RJ-45, SC/LC fibre

syllabus.title: Error detection and correction
topics: Types of errors; redundancy; Hamming distance and the detection and correction bounds
Simple and two-dimensional parity; checksums and the Internet checksum
Cyclic codes and CRC: generator polynomials, division in hardware with shift registers, standard CRCs
Hamming codes and burst-error handling with interleaving
Introduction to convolutional and Reed-Solomon codes as used in mobile and storage

syllabus.title: Data link control and flow control
topics: Framing: character count, byte stuffing, bit stuffing
Flow control: stop-and-wait, sliding window; efficiency and link utilisation
Error control with ARQ: stop-and-wait ARQ, go-back-N, selective repeat; sequence numbers
HDLC and PPP frame formats
Media access: ALOHA, CSMA, CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA; token passing; channelisation

syllabus.title: Switching
topics: Circuit switching: space and time division switches; the telephone network
Packet switching: datagram and virtual circuit; store-and-forward delay
Message switching; comparison of delay, setup and reliability
Structure of a switch and a router; from switching to networking

courses.title: Database Systems and Design
topics: Database environment and approaches
System concepts and architecture
Entity-Relationship model
Functional dependencies and normalisation
Installing and configuring database software
SELECT, restricting and sorting
Joins
Subqueries
Set operators
DDL: create and manage tables
courses.description: Designing relational databases from requirements to normalised schema, and querying them with the full power of SQL, with a working database server from the second week. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory database systems course.
modelledOn: Elmasri and Navathe, Fundamentals of Database Systems
Silberschatz, Korth and Sudarshan, Database System Concepts
Garcia-Molina, Ullman and Widom, Database Systems: The Complete Book
outcomes: Explain the database approach, the three-schema architecture and the components of a DBMS.
Model a domain as an entity-relationship diagram and map it to relational tables.
Apply functional dependencies to normalise a schema to 3NF and BCNF and judge when to denormalise.
Write SQL queries with filtering, sorting, joins, subqueries, set operators, grouping and window functions.
Create and manage tables, constraints, indexes, views and transactions with DDL and DCL.
Install, configure and administer a database server and connect an application to it.

syllabus.title: Database environment and approaches
topics: File-based systems and their problems; the database approach; data independence
Database users and roles; DBMS functions; advantages and costs
Relational, NoSQL and NewSQL landscape; where each fits
Example domains used all term: a university registry, a clinic, a mobile-money agent network

syllabus.title: System concepts and architecture
topics: Data models, schemas and instances; the three-schema architecture
DBMS languages (DDL, DML, DCL) and interfaces; client-server architecture
Installing and configuring database software: PostgreSQL or MySQL, users, ports, a first database
Tools: psql or mysql CLI, a graphical client, loading sample data

syllabus.title: The relational model
topics: Relations, attributes, tuples, domains; keys: super, candidate, primary, foreign
Integrity constraints: entity, referential, domain; NULL semantics
Relational algebra: select, project, join, union, difference, rename
Relational calculus in brief and how SQL relates to algebra

syllabus.title: Entity-Relationship modelling
topics: Entities, attributes (simple, composite, multivalued, derived), keys
Relationships, cardinality and participation constraints; weak entities
Enhanced ER: specialisation, generalisation, categories; UML class diagrams for data
Mapping ER to relational schemas step by step
Modelling workshop: from interview notes to an ER diagram for a clinic

syllabus.title: Functional dependencies and normalisation
topics: Update, insertion and deletion anomalies; design guidelines
Functional dependencies, Armstrong's axioms, closure, minimal cover
1NF, 2NF, 3NF and BCNF with worked decompositions; lossless join and dependency preservation
Multivalued dependencies and 4NF
When to denormalise for performance and reporting

syllabus.title: SQL: SELECT, restricting and sorting
topics: SELECT, DISTINCT, column aliases, expressions, string and date functions
WHERE with comparison, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE, IS NULL, logical operators
ORDER BY, LIMIT and OFFSET
Aggregates, GROUP BY and HAVING; CASE expressions

syllabus.title: Joins, subqueries and set operators
topics: Inner, left, right and full outer joins; self joins; cross joins; natural joins and USING
Single-row and multi-row subqueries; correlated subqueries; EXISTS and NOT EXISTS
Subqueries in FROM and SELECT; common table expressions; recursive queries for hierarchies
UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT
Window functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, running totals
Reading an execution plan and adding an index

syllabus.title: DDL: creating and managing tables
topics: CREATE TABLE with data types, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, NOT NULL, DEFAULT
ALTER TABLE, DROP, TRUNCATE; sequences and auto-increment
INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE; bulk loading from CSV
Views, indexes, schemas; GRANT and REVOKE

syllabus.title: Transactions, storage and administration
topics: ACID properties; COMMIT and ROLLBACK; isolation levels and anomalies
Locks and deadlocks; introduction to recovery and the log
Storage: pages, heap files, B+ tree and hash indexes
Backup, restore, users, roles and basic security configuration

syllabus.title: Databases in applications
topics: Connecting from Python or Java; prepared statements and SQL injection
Stored procedures, functions and triggers
Project: design, normalise, build and query a database for a real local organisation
Preview of NoSQL document and key-value stores

courses.title: Digital Logic Design
topics: Number systems, base conversion, complements, codes (BCD, Gray, error detecting/correcting)
Logic gates, universal gates, canonical and standard forms
Minimisation: Karnaugh maps (3-5 variables), Quine-McCluskey, NAND/NOR realisations
Combinational circuits: adders, subtractors, multipliers, mux/demux, encoders, decoders, code converters, comparators
Latches and flip-flops: SR, D, T, JK, master-slave, timing
Sequential circuits: counters, ring counters, shift registers
Memory devices: ROM, PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, RAM, PLA, PAL

modelledOn: Mano and Ciletti, Digital Design
Harris and Harris, Digital Design and Computer Architecture
Nand2Tetris: Building a Modern Computer from First Principles (hardware part)
outcomes: Convert between number systems and codes, and reason about overflow and signed arithmetic.
Specify, minimise and implement any combinational function with gates, muxes or ROM/PLA.
Analyse and design synchronous sequential circuits with flip-flops and finite state machines.
Reason about timing: propagation delay, setup and hold, clock period and glitches.
Build arithmetic units, registers and memories, and compose them into a simple datapath.

syllabus.title: Digital abstraction and number representation
topics: Why digital: noise margins, the static discipline, voltage levels for 0 and 1
Binary, octal, hexadecimal; base conversion; fixed-point fractions
Signed numbers: sign-magnitude, one's and two's complement; overflow detection
Codes: BCD, Gray code, ASCII and Unicode; unit-distance codes
Error detection and correction: parity, checksums, Hamming distance and Hamming(7,4)

syllabus.title: Boolean algebra and logic gates
topics: Axioms and theorems of Boolean algebra; duality; De Morgan's laws
Switching functions; truth tables; canonical sum-of-products and product-of-sums
Gate families: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR; universal gates
CMOS implementation of inverters and NAND gates; fan-in, fan-out, propagation delay
Logic families compared: TTL, CMOS; voltage levels and power

syllabus.title: Minimisation and multilevel implementation
topics: Algebraic simplification
Karnaugh maps for 2 to 5 variables; prime implicants, essential prime implicants, don't cares
Quine-McCluskey tabular method and the covering problem
Two-level versus multilevel logic; NAND-only and NOR-only realisations
Hazards and glitches; hazard-free design

syllabus.title: Combinational building blocks
topics: Design procedure: specification, truth table, minimisation, implementation, verification
Half and full adders, ripple-carry adders, carry-lookahead and carry-select adders
Subtractors and two's-complement add/subtract units; comparators
Multipliers: array multiplier and shift-and-add
Multiplexers, demultiplexers, encoders, priority encoders, decoders, code converters
Implementing functions with multiplexers and decoders; tri-state buffers and buses

syllabus.title: Latches, flip-flops and timing
topics: The bistable element; SR latch; gated D latch
Edge-triggered D flip-flop; master-slave construction; JK and T flip-flops
Characteristic and excitation tables; converting one flip-flop type to another
Timing: setup time, hold time, clock-to-Q, minimum clock period, metastability
Asynchronous inputs, synchronisers and debouncing

syllabus.title: Sequential circuits and finite state machines
topics: Registers, shift registers (SISO, SIPO, PISO, PIPO), ring and Johnson counters
Synchronous and asynchronous (ripple) counters; up/down and modulo-N counters
Moore and Mealy machines; state diagrams and state tables
FSM design procedure: state assignment, next-state logic, output logic
State reduction and equivalent states; one-hot encoding
Worked designs: sequence detector, vending machine, traffic-light controller

syllabus.title: Memory and programmable logic
topics: Memory organisation: address, data, word size; read and write cycles
ROM, PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, flash; SRAM and DRAM cells; refresh
Implementing combinational logic with ROM
PLA, PAL and the idea of programmable interconnect; introduction to FPGAs
Register files and simple RAM built from flip-flops

syllabus.title: From logic to a datapath
topics: Arithmetic logic unit: operation select, flags (zero, carry, overflow, negative)
Register transfer notation and control signals
A minimal datapath: registers, ALU, memory, program counter
Instruction execution as a sequence of register transfers (bridge to Computer Organisation and Architecture)

courses.title: Programming with C++
topics: Creating a program, std namespace, comments
Variables and constants
Expressions and statements
Program flow
Functions
Arrays
Pointers
Classes

Roberts, Programming Abstractions in C++
The C++ Core Guidelines

Security principles: least privilege, defence in depth, fail-safe defaults, separation of duties

syllabus.title: Addressing threats: backdoors, viruses, worms and malware
topics: Malware taxonomy: viruses, worms, trojans, backdoors, rootkits, ransomware, spyware, botnets; famous cases (Morris worm, Stuxnet, WannaCry)
Infection vectors: phishing, drive-by downloads, removable media, supply chain; social engineering
How antivirus and endpoint detection work: signatures, heuristics, behaviour, sandboxing; evasion
Safe malware analysis in an isolated lab: static and dynamic basics
Software vulnerabilities: buffer overflows, injection, race conditions; CVE and CVSS; patch management

syllabus.title: Password cracking and authentication
topics: Password storage: hashing, salting, slow hashes; what happens in a breach
Attacks: brute force, dictionary, rainbow tables, credential stuffing, spraying; John the Ripper and hashcat in the lab
Password policies that work; password managers; passphrases
Authentication factors; OTP, TOTP, SMS and its weaknesses, hardware keys, FIDO2/WebAuthn, biometrics
Single sign-on, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect, Kerberos; session management
Access control models: DAC, MAC, RBAC, ABAC

syllabus.title: Cryptography in practice
topics: Symmetric and asymmetric encryption, hashes, MACs and signatures as tools
TLS, VPNs, disk and file encryption, encrypted messaging; certificates and PKI
Common misuse: ECB, hard-coded keys, weak randomness, home-made crypto
Steganography and watermarking in brief

syllabus.title: Intrusion detection systems
topics: Host and network IDS/IPS; signature-based versus anomaly-based detection; false positives and negatives
Snort and Suricata rules; Zeek; OSSEC/Wazuh
Log management and SIEM; correlation and alerting
Deploying an IDS in the lab and detecting a scan and an exploit

syllabus.title: Firewalls and honeypots
topics: Firewall types: packet filtering, stateful, application-layer, next-generation; architectures (DMZ, screened subnet)
Writing rules: iptables/nftables, pfSense; web application firewalls
Honeypots and honeynets: low and high interaction, deception, legal issues
Network segmentation and zero-trust architecture

syllabus.title: Introduction to ethical hacking
topics: Legal and ethical framework: authorisation, scope, rules of engagement, Ghana's Cybersecurity Act
The penetration testing methodology: reconnaissance (OSINT), scanning (nmap), enumeration, vulnerability assessment (OpenVAS, Nessus), exploitation (Metasploit), post-exploitation, reporting
Web application testing with OWASP Top Ten: injection, broken authentication, XSS, IDOR; Burp Suite and OWASP ZAP
Wireless and social engineering assessments
Writing a penetration test report and remediation plan

syllabus.title: Network attacks and defences
topics: Sniffing, ARP spoofing, DNS spoofing, man-in-the-middle, session hijacking
Denial of service and DDoS: SYN floods, amplification; mitigation
Wireless attacks: WEP/WPA cracking, evil twins; securing Wi-Fi
Hardening hosts and networks; secure configuration baselines (CIS Benchmarks)

syllabus.title: Management of information security
topics: Security governance; roles (CISO), policies, standards, procedures, guidelines; security awareness training
Risk management: identification, assessment (qualitative and quantitative, ALE), treatment
Legal and regulatory: Data Protection Act 843, Cybersecurity Act 2020, PCI DSS, GDPR for international customers
Incident response planning and the incident life cycle

syllabus.title: Security management models, standards, audits and disaster recovery
topics: Models: ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and 27002 controls, NIST CSF and SP 800-53, COBIT; the Bell-LaPadula and Biba models
Security audits and compliance; vulnerability management programmes; security metrics
Business continuity and disaster recovery: BIA, RTO/RPO, backup strategies, hot/warm/cold sites, testing the plan
Capstone: a security assessment and ISMS plan for a small organisation

courses.title: Machine Learning
topics: Supervised and unsupervised learning
Linear and logistic regression
Decision trees and ensembles
Neural networks and backpropagation
Model evaluation and overfitting
Feature engineering
Ethics and bias in ML
courses.description: Learning from data with the mathematics made explicit: regression, classification, trees and ensembles, neural networks trained by backpropagation, unsupervised learning, rigorous evaluation, feature engineering and the ethics of deployed models, with every algorithm implemented from scratch before using a library. Taught to the depth of a leading machine learning course.
modelledOn: Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning
Murphy, Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning (introductory chapters)
outcomes: Formulate supervised and unsupervised learning problems and derive and implement the core algorithms with gradient descent.
Fit and regularise linear and logistic regression models and interpret their coefficients.
Train decision trees, random forests and gradient-boosted ensembles and explain why ensembles work.
Implement a neural network with backpropagation and train it with modern optimisers and regularisation.
Evaluate models with appropriate metrics, cross-validation and learning curves and diagnose bias and variance.
Engineer features for tabular, text and image data and assess fairness, bias and privacy before deployment.

syllabus.title: Supervised and unsupervised learning
topics: What learning from data means; supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised and reinforcement settings
Hypothesis spaces, loss functions, empirical risk minimisation; generalisation
Linear algebra, probability and calculus refresher as used in the course
Tooling: NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch; notebooks and experiment tracking

syllabus.title: Linear regression
topics: Least squares: closed form and gradient descent; batch, stochastic and mini-batch
Feature scaling, polynomial features, basis functions
Ridge and lasso regularisation; the bias-variance trade-off
Probabilistic view: maximum likelihood with Gaussian noise; Bayesian regression in brief
Predicting crop yield or house prices in Accra from tabular data

syllabus.title: Logistic regression and linear classifiers
topics: Logistic regression: sigmoid, cross-entropy loss, gradient, decision boundaries; multiclass with softmax
Generative versus discriminative: naive Bayes and Gaussian discriminant analysis
Support vector machines: margins, hinge loss, kernels
k-nearest neighbours and the curse of dimensionality

syllabus.title: Model evaluation, overfitting and model selection
topics: Train, validation and test splits; k-fold and stratified cross-validation; data leakage
Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC and PR curves, AUC, log loss, RMSE, MAE; imbalanced classes
Bias and variance; learning curves; underfitting and overfitting diagnosis
Hyperparameter search: grid, random, Bayesian; nested cross-validation
Statistical significance of model comparisons; reporting results honestly

syllabus.title: Decision trees and ensembles
topics: Decision trees: entropy, information gain, Gini, CART, pruning, handling continuous and missing values
Bagging and random forests; out-of-bag error; feature importance
Boosting: AdaBoost, gradient boosting, XGBoost and LightGBM; stacking
Why ensembles reduce variance; interpretability with SHAP and partial dependence

syllabus.title: Neural networks and backpropagation
topics: Perceptron to multilayer perceptron; activation functions; universal approximation
Backpropagation derived and implemented with NumPy; computational graphs and automatic differentiation
Optimisation: SGD with momentum, Adam, learning-rate schedules; initialisation; batch normalisation
Regularisation: weight decay, dropout, early stopping, data augmentation
Convolutional networks for images and recurrent networks and transformers for sequences, in brief; transfer learning
Training a classifier for cassava leaf disease images

syllabus.title: Unsupervised learning
topics: k-means, Gaussian mixture models and the EM algorithm; hierarchical and density-based clustering
Dimensionality reduction: PCA derived from variance maximisation and SVD; t-SNE and UMAP for visualisation
Anomaly detection; autoencoders in brief
Recommender systems: collaborative filtering and matrix factorisation

syllabus.title: Feature engineering and the ML pipeline
topics: Encoding categorical variables, scaling, binning, interactions, date features, handling missing data
Text features: bag of words, TF-IDF, word embeddings; image features and pretrained encoders
Feature selection: filter, wrapper, embedded methods
Pipelines, reproducibility, model versioning and deployment basics (serving a model behind an API)

syllabus.title: Learning theory and advanced topics
topics: PAC learning, VC dimension and generalisation bounds in brief
Online learning, active learning, semi-supervised learning
Reinforcement learning overview: bandits, Q-learning, policy gradients
Large language models and foundation models: what they are and how to use them responsibly

syllabus.title: Ethics and bias in machine learning
topics: Sources of bias: data, labels, proxies, feedback loops; fairness definitions and their incompatibility
Explainability and accountability; model cards and datasheets
Privacy: differential privacy and federated learning in brief; data protection law
Case studies: credit scoring, facial recognition, predictive policing; deploying ML responsibly in Ghana
Capstone: a complete project with a model card and fairness audit

courses.title: Operating Systems
topics: Introduction to operating systems
Memory management
Process management, concurrency and synchronisation
File systems
I/O system
Virtual machines
Multiple processor systems
Mobile operating systems
courses.description: How an operating system virtualises the processor and memory, lets programs share safely, stores data persistently and talks to devices, learned by reading, modifying and measuring a real teaching kernel. Taught to the depth of a leading operating systems course.
modelledOn: Arpaci-Dusseau, Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
Silberschatz, Galvin and Gagne, Operating System Concepts
Tanenbaum and Bos, Modern Operating Systems
The xv6 teaching operating system and its commentary
outcomes: Explain the structure of an operating system, system calls, kernel and user modes, and the boot process.
Describe process and thread life cycles and implement and evaluate CPU scheduling algorithms.
Write correct concurrent programs with locks, semaphores, condition variables and monitors, and detect and prevent deadlock.
Analyse memory management with paging, segmentation, virtual memory and page replacement.
Explain file system design, disk scheduling, I/O subsystems and device drivers.
Describe virtual machines, multiprocessor operating systems and the design of mobile operating systems.

syllabus.title: Introduction to operating systems
topics: What an OS does: abstraction, virtualisation, resource management, protection; history from batch to cloud and mobile
Kernel and user mode, system calls, traps and interrupts; the boot sequence
OS structures: monolithic, layered, microkernel, modules, exokernel; Linux, Windows and xv6 compared
Shell, processes and system programming in C: fork, exec, wait, pipes, signals
Building and running xv6 in an emulator; reading kernel code

syllabus.title: Process management
topics: Processes: states, PCB, context switch, creation and termination; the process tree
Threads: user and kernel threads, pthreads, thread pools; why threads
CPU scheduling: FCFS, SJF, SRTF, priority, round robin, multilevel feedback queues; metrics and Gantt charts
Real-time scheduling (RM, EDF), proportional share and the Linux CFS
Implementing a scheduler in xv6 and measuring turnaround and response time

syllabus.title: Concurrency and synchronisation
topics: Race conditions, critical sections, atomicity; Peterson's algorithm and hardware primitives (test-and-set, compare-and-swap)
Locks, spinlocks, semaphores, condition variables, monitors; producer-consumer, readers-writers, dining philosophers
Deadlock: conditions, resource allocation graphs, prevention, avoidance (banker's algorithm), detection and recovery
Concurrency bugs: atomicity and order violations; lock-free structures in brief
Inter-process communication: shared memory, message passing, pipes, sockets

syllabus.title: Memory management
topics: Address spaces, address binding, logical versus physical addresses; base and bounds
Contiguous allocation and fragmentation; segmentation; free-space management (first fit, best fit, buddy, slab)
Paging: page tables, TLBs, multi-level and inverted page tables; address translation worked examples
Virtual memory: demand paging, page faults, copy-on-write; replacement (FIFO, LRU, clock, optimal); thrashing and the working set
Memory in xv6: page tables, allocation, implementing lazy allocation

syllabus.title: File systems
topics: Files, directories, links, permissions; the file system interface and the VFS layer
Storage layout: inodes, extents, bitmaps, directories; FAT, ext4, NTFS compared
Crash consistency: fsck, journaling, copy-on-write (ZFS, Btrfs), log-structured file systems
Caching, buffering, read-ahead; disk scheduling (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN); SSDs and flash translation layers
RAID and reliability; network file systems

syllabus.title: I/O system
topics: I/O hardware: controllers, ports, buses, polling, interrupts, DMA
The I/O subsystem: device drivers, character and block devices, buffering, spooling
Writing a simple device driver; interrupt handling in the kernel
Clocks, timers and power management

syllabus.title: Protection, security and virtual machines
topics: Protection domains, access control lists, capabilities; user authentication and privilege
OS security: buffer overflows, privilege escalation, sandboxing, address-space randomisation
Virtual machines: hypervisors (type 1 and 2), trap-and-emulate, paravirtualisation, hardware support, nested page tables
Containers: namespaces, cgroups, images; VMs versus containers

syllabus.title: Multiple processor systems and mobile operating systems
topics: Multiprocessor scheduling, load balancing, processor affinity, cache coherence effects, NUMA
Distributed and cluster operating systems in brief
Mobile operating systems: Android architecture (Linux kernel, ART, Binder, app sandbox), iOS; power management, app life cycle, permissions
Case study: the Linux kernel and how to contribute; the future of operating systems

courses.title: Wireless Communication
topics: Wireless communication systems, 1G-4G standards
Modulation schemes
Statistical channel models, narrowband and wideband fading
Cellular concepts and system design, frequency reuse, SIR, capacity
Quality of service, trunking
Digital modulation and detection in AWGN, error probabilities
Coding for wireless channels
Multiple antenna systems, diversity, MIMO, OFDM
TDMA, FDMA, CDMA
MATLAB-style simulation
courses.description: The physics and engineering of mobile radio: from the generations of cellular standards through channel models, cellular design, digital modulation and coding in fading channels, multiple antennas and OFDM, and multiple access, with every link simulated and its error rate measured. Taught to the depth of a leading wireless communications course.
modelledOn: Goldsmith, Wireless Communications
Rappaport, Wireless Communications: Principles and Practice
Tse and Viswanath, Fundamentals of Wireless Communication
Molisch, Wireless Communications
outcomes: Trace the evolution from 1G to 5G and explain the architecture and key technologies of each generation.
Model path loss, shadowing and multipath fading and classify channels as narrowband or wideband, slow or fast.
Design a cellular layout with frequency reuse and compute signal-to-interference ratio, capacity and trunking performance.
Derive error probabilities for digital modulation in AWGN and fading channels and simulate them.
Explain channel coding, diversity, MIMO and OFDM and quantify their gains.
Compare TDMA, FDMA, CDMA and OFDMA and simulate a complete wireless link in MATLAB or Python.

syllabus.title: Wireless communication systems and standards
topics: History: from Marconi to 5G; 1G AMPS, 2G GSM and IS-95, 2.5G GPRS/EDGE, 3G UMTS/CDMA2000, 4G LTE, 5G NR and what 6G research targets
Cellular network architecture: mobiles, base stations, core network, handover, roaming, SIM and authentication
Spectrum: allocation, licensing, Ghana's NCA bands, unlicensed bands (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, LoRa)
Other wireless systems: satellite, WLAN, WPAN, microwave links; coverage in rural Ghana
Simulation environment: MATLAB or Python with NumPy and SciPy

syllabus.title: Modulation schemes and the radio link
topics: Analog modulation review: AM, FM; the transmitter and receiver chain; mixers, filters, amplifiers
Digital modulation overview: ASK, FSK, PSK, QAM; bandwidth efficiency and power efficiency
Pulse shaping, intersymbol interference, raised-cosine filters, eye diagrams
Link budget: transmit power, antenna gain, path loss, noise figure, receiver sensitivity

syllabus.title: Statistical channel models: narrowband and wideband fading
topics: Large-scale propagation: free space, two-ray, log-distance path loss, empirical models (Okumura-Hata, COST 231); log-normal shadowing
Small-scale multipath: delay spread, coherence bandwidth, Doppler spread, coherence time
Narrowband fading: Rayleigh and Rician distributions; level crossing rate and fade duration
Wideband channels: tapped delay line models, power delay profile, frequency-selective fading
Classifying channels: flat versus frequency selective, slow versus fast; simulating Rayleigh fading (Jakes model)

syllabus.title: Cellular concepts and system design
topics: The cellular concept: cells, clusters, frequency reuse, reuse distance and the cluster size
Co-channel and adjacent-channel interference; signal-to-interference ratio versus cluster size
Capacity: channels per cell, spectral efficiency; improving capacity with sectoring, cell splitting, microcells
Handover strategies, power control, mobility management
Designing a cellular layout for a Ghanaian town with given traffic and coverage targets

syllabus.title: Quality of service and trunking
topics: Traffic theory: Erlangs, offered load, grade of service
Erlang B and Erlang C formulas; blocked-calls-cleared versus queued systems; trunking efficiency
QoS parameters for voice, data and video; delay, jitter, loss; scheduling in LTE
Dimensioning a cell's channels for a target blocking probability

syllabus.title: Digital modulation and detection in AWGN; error probabilities
topics: Signal space representation; matched filter and correlation receivers; maximum likelihood detection
Error probabilities in AWGN for BPSK, QPSK, M-PSK, M-QAM, FSK; the Q-function and union bound
Performance in fading: average BER in Rayleigh fading and the diversity order; outage probability
Synchronisation and channel estimation in brief
Monte Carlo BER simulation and comparison with theory

syllabus.title: Coding for wireless channels
topics: Channel capacity (Shannon) for AWGN and fading channels; coding gain
Block codes (Hamming, Reed-Solomon), convolutional codes and Viterbi decoding; interleaving against bursts
Turbo codes, LDPC and polar codes as used in 3G, 4G and 5G
Hybrid ARQ and adaptive modulation and coding

syllabus.title: Multiple antenna systems: diversity, MIMO, OFDM
topics: Diversity: time, frequency, space; selection, equal-gain and maximal-ratio combining
MIMO: spatial multiplexing, capacity scaling, space-time codes (Alamouti), beamforming, massive MIMO in 5G
OFDM: orthogonal subcarriers, IFFT/FFT implementation, cyclic prefix, PAPR; OFDM in Wi-Fi, LTE and 5G
Simulating an OFDM link over a frequency-selective channel

syllabus.title: Multiple access: TDMA, FDMA, CDMA and beyond
topics: FDMA, TDMA and their use in 1G and GSM; frame structures
CDMA: spreading codes, processing gain, near-far problem and power control, RAKE receiver; IS-95 and UMTS
OFDMA and SC-FDMA in LTE; NOMA and random access (ALOHA, CSMA) for Wi-Fi and IoT
Capacity comparison of multiple access schemes
Capstone: a MATLAB-style end-to-end simulation of a cellular link with fading, coding, modulation and multiple access

courses.title: Big Data and Parallel Computing

MapReduce and distributed file systems
Spark-style dataflow
Threads, locks and parallel speed-up
GPU and SIMD concepts
Stream processing
Scaling and cost
courses.description: Computing on data too large or too slow for one core: shared-memory parallelism with threads and locks, SIMD and GPUs, and distributed data processing with MapReduce, Spark-style dataflow and stream processing, always measuring speed-up, scaling and cost. Taught to the depth of a leading parallel and big-data systems course.
modelledOn: Leskovec, Rajaraman and Ullman, Mining of Massive Datasets
Zaharia and Chambers, Spark: The Definitive Guide
Pacheco and Malensek, An Introduction to Parallel Programming
Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications
outcomes: Characterise big data problems and choose between scaling up, scaling out and smarter algorithms.
Write correct multithreaded programs with locks and lock-free techniques and measure speed-up against Amdahl's and Gustafson's laws.
Explain SIMD and GPU execution models and write a simple data-parallel kernel.
Design MapReduce jobs over a distributed file system and reason about shuffles, partitioning and fault tolerance.
Build Spark-style dataflow pipelines with RDDs and DataFrames and tune them.
Process unbounded streams with windows and exactly-once semantics and estimate the cost of a data platform.

syllabus.title: Characteristics of big data
topics: Volume, velocity, variety, veracity, value; where big data comes from (telecoms, mobile money, sensors, the web)
Why single machines fail: memory, disk and network limits; latency and throughput
The landscape: Hadoop ecosystem, Spark, cloud data platforms, streaming systems
Storage formats: CSV, JSON, Avro, Parquet, ORC; compression and columnar layout

syllabus.title: Parallel computing foundations
topics: Flynn's taxonomy; shared memory versus distributed memory; task and data parallelism
Speed-up, efficiency, Amdahl's law, Gustafson's law, scalability (strong and weak scaling)
Parallel algorithm design: decomposition, communication, agglomeration, mapping
Benchmarking methodology and reporting

syllabus.title: Threads, locks and parallel speed-up
topics: Threads in C/C++ (pthreads), Java and Python (and the GIL); OpenMP pragmas for loops
Data races, mutexes, condition variables, barriers, atomics; memory models and visibility
Deadlock, livelock, contention, false sharing, load imbalance
Parallel patterns: map, reduce, scan, pipeline, work stealing, fork-join; thread pools
Lock-free queues and compare-and-swap; measuring speed-up on matrix multiply and word count

syllabus.title: GPU and SIMD concepts
topics: Vector instructions (SSE, AVX, NEON) and auto-vectorisation
GPU architecture: streaming multiprocessors, warps, memory hierarchy; CUDA and OpenCL programming model
Writing a vector add and a reduction kernel; occupancy, coalescing, divergence
GPUs for machine learning and scientific computing; using GPUs through NumPy-like libraries

syllabus.title: Distributed file systems and MapReduce
topics: GFS/HDFS design: blocks, replication, name node, fault tolerance
The MapReduce model: map, shuffle, sort, reduce; combiners and partitioners; the execution framework and stragglers
Algorithms in MapReduce: word count, inverted index, joins, matrix multiplication, PageRank
Limitations of MapReduce and the move to in-memory dataflow
Running jobs on a local cluster or a free cloud tier

syllabus.title: Spark-style dataflow
topics: RDDs: transformations, actions, lineage, lazy evaluation, persistence
DataFrames and Spark SQL; the Catalyst optimiser; joins, aggregations, window functions
Partitioning, shuffles, broadcast joins, caching; reading the Spark UI; tuning memory and parallelism
Machine learning at scale with MLlib; graph processing with GraphX or Pregel-style models
Dask and other dataflow engines compared

syllabus.title: Stream processing
topics: Bounded versus unbounded data; event time versus processing time; watermarks
Messaging backbones: Kafka topics, partitions, consumer groups
Windows (tumbling, sliding, session), state, exactly-once semantics; Flink and Spark Structured Streaming
Streaming algorithms: sampling, Bloom filters, count-min sketch, HyperLogLog
Real-time fraud detection on a mobile-money transaction stream

syllabus.title: Data platforms, scaling and cost
topics: Data lakes, lakehouses and warehouses; orchestration with Airflow; schema evolution
Scaling strategies: partitioning, replication, autoscaling, spot instances
Cost models: cloud pricing, storage versus compute, egress; total cost of a pipeline in dollars and cedis
Performance versus cost trade-offs; when a single big machine with DuckDB or Polars is enough

syllabus.title: Capstone
topics: End-to-end project: ingest, process in batch and streaming, store and query a large public dataset
Measuring and reporting speed-up, scaling and cost
Reliability, monitoring and data quality in production pipelines
Presentation and code review

courses.title: Blockchain and Distributed Ledgers
topics: Hashing and Merkle trees
Blocks, chains and immutability
Proof of work and proof of stake
Wallets, keys and transactions
Smart contracts
Use cases: land registry, supply chain, payments
Limitations and regulation
courses.description: Blockchains built up from their parts: hashes and Merkle trees, blocks and chains, consensus by proof of work and proof of stake, keys, wallets and transactions, smart contracts, and a clear-eyed look at real use cases, limits and regulation, with a small blockchain implemented and a contract deployed to a test network. Taught to the depth of a leading blockchain technologies course.
modelledOn: Narayanan, Bonneau, Felten, Miller and Goldfeder, Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies
Antonopoulos, Mastering Bitcoin
Antonopoulos and Wood, Mastering Ethereum
Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
outcomes: Explain and implement the cryptographic building blocks of a blockchain: hashes, Merkle trees, digital signatures.
Describe how blocks, chains, forks and confirmations give tamper-evidence and how a longest-chain rule resolves conflicts.
Compare proof of work, proof of stake and permissioned consensus and analyse their security and energy assumptions.
Create keys and wallets, construct and verify transactions, and explain the UTXO and account models.
Write, test and deploy a smart contract and identify common vulnerabilities.
Evaluate blockchain proposals for land registry, supply chain and payments against simpler alternatives, and summarise the regulatory position.

syllabus.title: Hashing and Merkle trees
topics: Cryptographic hash properties; SHA-256 and Keccak; hash pointers and tamper-evident lists
Merkle trees: construction, proofs of inclusion, light clients
Digital signatures with ECDSA and secp256k1; public keys as identities
Commitments and puzzles; implementing hashes, Merkle proofs and signatures in code

syllabus.title: Blocks, chains and immutability
topics: Block structure: header, previous hash, Merkle root, nonce, timestamp, difficulty
Chaining, forks, orphan blocks, confirmations; why rewriting history is expensive
Peer-to-peer networking: gossip, block and transaction propagation, nodes and miners
Building a minimal blockchain in Python or JavaScript and attacking it
Distributed ledgers versus databases: what immutability does and does not give you

syllabus.title: Proof of work and proof of stake
topics: The double-spend problem and Byzantine agreement among strangers; the Nakamoto consensus
Proof of work: mining, difficulty adjustment, hash rate, pools, 51 percent attacks, selfish mining, energy consumption
Proof of stake: validators, staking, slashing, finality (Casper, Tendermint); nothing-at-stake and long-range attacks
Permissioned consensus: PBFT, Raft-based ledgers (Hyperledger Fabric)
Comparing security, decentralisation, throughput and energy; the scalability trilemma

syllabus.title: Wallets, keys and transactions
topics: Key generation, addresses, hierarchical deterministic wallets, seed phrases, custody and loss
Transactions: inputs and outputs (UTXO model), scripts, fees, mempool; the account model in Ethereum
Constructing, signing and verifying a transaction by hand; multisignature and time locks
Exchanges, stablecoins, and how cedis move into and out of crypto; the risks of custodial services

syllabus.title: Smart contracts
topics: Ethereum: the EVM, gas, accounts, state; Solidity basics: types, functions, events, modifiers
Writing, testing (Hardhat or Foundry) and deploying a contract to a test network; interacting from a web page
Token standards (ERC-20, ERC-721) and decentralised applications; oracles
Vulnerabilities: reentrancy (The DAO), integer issues, access control, front-running; auditing and formal verification in brief
Layer-2 scaling: payment channels, rollups; cross-chain bridges

syllabus.title: Use cases: land registry, supply chain, payments
topics: Land registry: Ghana's land title problems, the Bitland pilot, what a ledger can and cannot fix (garbage in, legal recognition)
Supply chain provenance: cocoa and pharmaceuticals; the oracle problem; IBM Food Trust lessons
Payments and remittances: cross-border transfers, stablecoins, central bank digital currencies (e-Cedi), mobile money comparison
Identity, voting, academic credentials and other proposals; a decision framework: do you need a blockchain?
Enterprise ledgers: Hyperledger Fabric and permissioned deployments

syllabus.title: Limitations and regulation
topics: Limits: throughput, latency, energy, privacy on public ledgers, key loss, upgradeability, governance
Scams, fraud and consumer harm; AML/KYC and the travel rule
Regulation: Bank of Ghana and SEC positions, the e-Cedi, international approaches (MiCA, FATF)
Capstone: a complete decentralised application with a report on whether a blockchain was the right choice

courses.title: Cloud Computing
topics: Roots of cloud computing
Deployment models and service models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS)
Characteristics of cloud computing
Architecture layers and methodologies
Security in the cloud
Service selection and SMI attributes
Cloud economics: provisioning, cost optimisation, multitenancy, monitoring
Google, Azure and AWS platforms
Service management

NIST SP 800-145 The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing and NIST SP 500-292 Cloud Computing Reference Architecture
AWS Cloud Practitioner, Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) and Google Cloud Digital Leader objectives
Erl, Mahmood and Puttini, Cloud Computing: Concepts, Technology and Architecture
